messages.subject: plotting a function
parts:
Hello everybody

I would like to plot a function in shiny. The goal is that I can define this function in a textInput-Box in the ui.R-file, but that doesn't work. If I define the function (for example sin(x^2)) in the server.R-file in the renderPlot-environment it works properly, but I can't get it from the ui.R-file... I tried to convert the textInput (with as.function() a.s.o.) but I didn't suceed. Has anybody an idea how can I do this? How I have to define this function? Thanks a lot. 

Marco

messages.author: e04bb64c7c0b4424
messages.subject: Re: plotting a function
parts:
I would suggest using eval(parse()). I am assuming you are adding just giving a small mathematical piece for use in manipulating your plotted data. If this is true you could do : 


### input$function <- "sin(dt^2)"  is passed from the ui.R file
library(evaluate)
library(ggplot2)
  output$plot<- renderPlot({
    data<- data.frame(x=c(1:10),y= c(21:30))
    eval(parse(text=
                 paste0(  "func<- function(dt){
                             ",input$function,"
                          }")))
    
    ggplot(as.data.frame(func(data)), aes(x=x, y=y, color=x)) + geom_point()
 })

I ran it on my computer just fine. The evaluate function will load the function from parse into the environment as if it was loaded from another file. Although, I am not sure if this is the most efficient way of doing what you want. I myself have recently asked a similar question in regards to this issue but I hope this is what you are asking for. Good Luck!

Amber

messages.subject: Re: plotting a function
parts: eval(parse()) is indeed how you would do this, BUT it is only suitable for use when the person who is using the Shiny app is also the person who launched the Shiny app--in other words, for single-user use on one's own computer, not for hosting via ShinyApps.io or Shiny Server. The reason is because eval(parse()) will let the user execute arbitrary code on the machine that's running server.R--for example, "unlink('/', recursive = TRUE)".
